promo-banner is highly discriminating (100% vs 40%): without the skill's mechanical 'spacing segment -> spacing prop, match by variable name not pixel value' rule, the baseline invented its own responsive CSS solution encoding both resolved pixel values via a media query — exactly the anti-pattern rule 4 exists to prevent, and a natural mistake for a model with no Hearth-specific guidance to make.

action-row doesn't discriminate (100% both): the eval prompt's own wording ('Implement them exactly as specified — no more, no less') already telegraphs the correct answer, so it doesn't actually test whether a model would invent a colour variant unprompted from the screenshot-shading detail alone. Recommend dropping that instruction in a future revision so the eval tests the instinct, not just instruction-following.

With-skill runs took about 4x longer (780s vs 190s mean) and roughly 1.6x the tokens (77k vs 49k mean) than baseline, driven mostly by the promo-banner run's live MCP docs-list/docs-show verification calls.
